Skin Disease Detection is a Machine Learning and Computer Vision project by Muhammad Awais. It analyzes a skin image and predicts one of seven supported skin-disease categories, returning a prediction with a confidence score. The project uses TensorFlow and EfficientNetB0 with a Flask backend. It is intended for educational and research purposes, not medical diagnosis.

answer: Skin Disease Detection is an AI-based Computer Vision project that uses an EfficientNetB0 model to classify skin images into seven supported categories. The project uses TensorFlow for the model and Flask for the backend. The backend processes an uploaded image and returns the predicted category with a confidence score. It is an educational/research project and should not be used as a medical diagnosis.

keywords: what model does skin disease detection use
answer: The Skin Disease Detection project uses EfficientNetB0. It is implemented with TensorFlow and was selected as a relatively efficient deep learning architecture for image classification.

keywords: technologies used in skin disease detection
answer: The main technologies used in Skin Disease Detection are Python, TensorFlow 2.20, EfficientNetB0, and Flask. The model was developed and tested using CPU-based Python 3.12.
The current portfolio version of Skin Disease Detection uses EfficientNetB0 V2 and has a reported accuracy of 52.38% on the project's evaluation set.

The Skin Disease Detection project uses a 700-image subset of the ISIC 2018 Task 3 dataset. It contains 100 images for each of seven classes. The data was split into 490 training images, 105 validation images, and 105 evaluation images.
The seven supported classes are actinic keratosis (akiec), basal cell carcinoma (bcc), benign keratosis (bkl), dermatofibroma (df), melanoma (mel), melanocytic nevus (nv), and vascular lesion (vasc).

The Skin Disease Detection backend uses Flask. A user uploads a skin image, the Flask backend processes the image, sends it to the trained EfficientNetB0 model, and returns the predicted category together with a confidence score.

Key features include image-based classification, seven supported categories, EfficientNetB0 inference, confidence scores, and a Flask backend for processing predictions.
